To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) adaptive regulation of learning is associated with more positive academic outcomes, (2) adaptive and maladaptive regulatory strategies are associated with different types of self reported learning difficulties, (3) maladaptive regulation is associated with lower academic performance, (4) maladaptive regulation of learning is more common than adaptive regulation, and (5) adaptive regulation of emotions and adaptive regulation of learning are positively associated

(a) adaptive regulation of learning is associated with higher achievement; (b) adaptive regulation of study is associated with higher academic self-efficacy; and (c) adaptive regulation is associated with higher levels of self-reported motivation.

Adaptive regulation of learning can be distinguished from maladaptive regulation of learning by: 1) using an online diary to examine students' adaptive and self handicapping responses to challenges in the context of a webquest; and 2) using multimodal data (e.g. think-alouds, video) to examine adaptive and self handicapped responses to a webquest.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how students' SRL processes can either support their own development and academic achievement or inhibit it.
understanding adaptive regulation of learning, as well as the conditions that may lead to maladaptive patterns and processes.
understanding adaptive and maladaptive SRL patterns and processes, and how these patterns and processes can be fostered in educational contexts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regulation of learning is a complex process that is adaptive and maladaptive at different times and in different contexts.
adaptive regulation of learning is a complex and dynamic process that is not always linear, and can involve maladaptive responses that are adaptive for short term goals.
the regulation of learning is a complex, multi-dimensional, and dynamic process that can be adaptive or maladaptive depending on a student's goal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regulation of learning can be both adaptive and maladaptive.
adaptive and maladaptive regulatory patterns and processes are complex and multifaceted, and that there are many factors that influence how students regulate their learning.
adaptive SRL is a complex process involving the interplay between students' metacognitive awareness, motivation, and emotion regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students can exhibit both adaptive and maladaptive SRL skills in their learning.

students' adaptive regulation of their own learning can be captured through a variety of methods, and that this regulation is not always a linear process, and may include periods of both adaptive and maladaptive responses.
adaptive and maladaptive SRL is not simply a matter of students' cognitive abilities but also involves students' social and emotional skills.
